desk.headline: Record adjusted EPS of $2.85 (ex-notables), up 22% and a beat; no new numeric outlook, yearly targets on track

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted, excluding notable items (revenue = total adjusted revenues)

results: Adjusted earnings rose 12% to $1.8bn; excluding the yearly actuarial review, adjusted EPS was a record $2.85, up 22%.
GAAP net income nearly tripled to $2.4bn, mostly from derivative gains as U.S. interest rates rose.
Every segment grew revenue; Group Benefits earnings rose 15% on good underwriting and Asia 17% before one-offs.
Higher returns from private equity and similar investments lifted adjusted investment income 10% to $6.0bn.
About $1bn went back to shareholders in buybacks and dividends; holding company cash was $3.4bn.

guidance.summary: MetLife gave no new numeric outlook. It said it is on track for its 2026 free cash flow and direct expense ratio targets, and the CFO stood by the 65–75% free cash flow target.

points: The CEO stressed breadth: no single business drove the record quarter.
Disability claims were more severe, but recoveries and claim handling kept results within the target range.
Unusually good working-age mortality may slowly normalise, playing out over years rather than quarters.
Management expects AI-driven productivity and cost control to push the expense ratio lower over time.
Capital use stays focused on organic growth and selective deals, alongside buybacks and dividends.

watch: Whether Group Benefits mortality and disability results stay this favourable.
Variable investment income, which can swing with private-market returns.
Pace of buybacks and any 2027 targets set at the year-end results.
